text:
tara: FYI — during a quickstart onboarding demo the Node quickstart sample app replayed a POST after a simulated 429 and caused duplicate DB writes. steps: start quickstart, hit rate limit, retry happens and we see two create_user calls.
ben: which quickstart? quickstart-js? can you paste the snippet you ran?
tara: quickstart-js. minimal repro:
```js
// quickstart.js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retry: { maxRetries: 3, jitter: true } });
await client.createUser({ name: "demo" });
```
lucy: looks like there's no idempotency key being set by the sample. python SDK adds X-Idempotency-Key for create helpers by default; node sample doesn't — parity gap.
ben: oh — that explains duplicates. node SDK currently leaves idempotency to the app. are we comfortable adding auto-idempotency for non-streaming POST helpers? any safety concerns?
sam: streaming endpoints are a no-go for auto-idempotency. also note jitter implementation matters — uniform jitter can cause retries to cluster and still hit the same hotspot. recommend full (exponential) jitter.
ben: noted. proposal: 1) node-sdk default autoIdempotency = true for high-level helpers (can opt-out), 2) change jitter strategy to full-jitter (rand(0, base * 2 ** attempt)), 3) update quickstart sample to set header when autoIdempotency disabled. i'll open a GH issue + PR for samples + SDK.
tara: can you also update onboarding docs to call out the behavior and show a helper util? users shouldn't have to know internal retry semantics during demos.
lucy: agreed, and add a test in the e2e harness that forces 429 from the stubbed gateway and asserts only one side-effect when idempotency key present.
ben: opening issue and assigning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4789 — PR coming. tagging @ben for follow-up.
issue-bot: created issue #4789 in redwood-inference/sdk: "node quickstart: auto-idempotency + jitter parity" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4789
tara: awesome, thanks. quick checklist for the PR: update quickstart sample, add a small util `ensureIdempotencyKey(req)` in examples, switch jitter impl in node-sdk retry module, and add e2e test.
sam: small caveat — we need to make sure kebab-case header name X-Idempotency-Key is documented in API contract and not accidentally stripped by proxies. shout if you need infra help reproducing via the rate-limiter.
ben: will sync with infra if needed. assigning the SDK work to myself and sample updates to docs.
tara: :thumbsup: keeping this thread as the single-source for the onboarding fallout. ping me if PR needs a quick review for the demo flow.
